title: Sosulski et al. 2019 — Online Optimization of Stimulation Speed in an Auditory Brain-Computer Interface under Time Constraints
description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an auditory oddball (P300) task with target (1000 Hz) and non-target (500 Hz) tones at stimulus onset asynchronies between 60 and 600 ms. The study compared random search and Bayesian optimization for selecting each individual's best stimulation speed in a closed-loop auditory BCI. The protocol had an optimization part and a validation part, and the target measure was classification performance of a regularized LDA. The data are 31-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz with a BrainProducts BrainAmp DC amplifier, using passive Ag/AgCl electrodes with a nose reference. Each trial presented 15 target and 75 non-target tones. In the optimization part, four strategies (AUC-ucb, AUC-rand, P300-ucb, P300-rand) each had 20 minutes to find the best SOA. In the validation part, the resulting SOAs and a fixed 60 ms SOA were each tested in 20 trials. Features were mean amplitudes in 5 time intervals across all channels, classified with shrinkage rLDA and 13-fold cross-validation.
